<h1>Note arps</h1>

Note arps store an 8-step pitch pattern per sequencer row. Every time a row's
trigger fires, the row plays the next note in its pattern, then wraps back to
the start when it reaches the end of the pattern's length.

By default each row's pattern is one note long, and the eight rows form a
scale. From here you can take that in three directions:

- **Arpeggiate.** Give a row a few notes and put a trig on every step, and you
  get a classic arp.
- **Sequence beyond eight notes.** The pattern advances on triggers, not on the
  clock, so a three-note pattern against four trigs takes three bars to come
  back round. Lengths that don't divide into each other give you lines that
  take a long time to repeat.
- **Pick a different eight notes.** Leave every row at one note and change
  that note, and the sequencer plays whatever eight pitches you choose instead
  of the scale.

---

## What You See

### Left Hand Launchpad

The pattern overview. Each row shows the length of that row's note pattern,
one lit pad per step. Each step has its own colour, and the same colours mark
that step's note on the right hand Launchpad, so you can also see the shape of
the pattern at a glance.

### Right Hand Launchpad

The isomorphic keyboard for the row you have selected (the last row you
pressed on the left). Each step of that row lights its note in the step's
colour, so you can see which note each step plays.

Every pad is a note of the current scale, rising upwards and rightwards, with
each row of the pad starting a fourth above the row below. The keyboard covers
four octaves, and the slate-grey pads mark the root notes so you always have
landmarks. The top-right pad is the rest pad: a step set to rest shows in
beige, on both Launchpads.

---

## Set a Pattern's Length

On the left hand Launchpad, **hold SHIFT and press a pad**, or simply
**double-tap a pad**, to set the pattern's length. That row's length becomes
the column you pressed: column 1 for a single note, column 8 for all eight.

Steps beyond the new length go dark straight away.

---

## Edit the Pattern

Editing takes two presses, one on each Launchpad:

1. **Press a pad on the LHS LP** to select that position in the note pattern.
2. **Press a pad on the RHS LP** to select the note for that position in the
   note pattern. Press the top-right pad instead and you get a **rest**.

---

## Preset Figures

Hold **MUTE** and press a pad on the LHS LP to write a ready-made figure to all
eight rows of the sequencer. The pads form a grid: the row you press picks the
shape, and the column picks the interval between its notes, so every shape
comes in every interval.

| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reset | seconds | thirds | fourths | fifths | sixths | sevenths | octaves |

Each figure is built around the row's own note: rising figures start on it,
falling figures end on it. A pedal tone is a note the figure keeps returning
to: the row's own note in rising figures, a high note in falling ones.

The table below shows each shape written to the bottom row, with the interval
set to seconds (column 2). The other columns stretch the same shape wider.

- **Scale steps** counts up the scale from the row's own note: 0 is the row's
  note, 1 the next note up, and 7 the same note an octave higher.
- **In C minor** shows the same figure as notes, for a bottom row on C.

| Row | Shape | Scale steps | In C minor |
|-----|-------|-------------|------------|
| 8 | Up | 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 | C D E♭ F G A♭ B♭ C |
| 7 | Double up | 0 0 1 1 2 2 3 3 | C C D D E♭ E♭ F F |
| 6 | Up with a pedal tone | 0 1 0 2 0 3 0 4 | C D C E♭ C F C G |
| 5 | Double up with a pedal tone | 0 0 1 1 0 0 2 2 | C C D D C C E♭ E♭ |
| 4 | Double down with a pedal tone | 2 2 1 1 2 2 0 0 | E♭ E♭ D D E♭ E♭ C C |
| 3 | Down with a pedal tone | 4 3 4 2 4 1 4 0 | G F G E♭ G D G C |
| 2 | Double down | 3 3 2 2 1 1 0 0 | F F E♭ E♭ D D C C |
| 1 | Down | 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 | C B♭ A♭ G F E♭ D C |

Wide intervals run out of keyboard, so their figures are shorter and repeat to
fill all eight steps.

To pick a figure, combine the two. For example:

- **Fifths up with a pedal tone**: hold MUTE and press row 6, column 5. On a
  bottom row on C minor that writes C G C D C A♭ C E♭: the C keeps coming back
  while the line between climbs a fifth at a time.
- **Thirds double down**: hold MUTE and press row 2, column 3. On the same row
  that writes B♭ B♭ G G E♭ E♭ C C: a C minor chord falling a third at a time,
  each note played twice.

The pad flashes to confirm. Two things to know:

- **A preset does not set lengths.** A row one note long still plays one note.
  Set your lengths first, then pick a figure.
- **A preset replaces every step**, including any rests. Put the figure down
  first, then add rests.

**Column 1** (any row) resets the whole sequencer: every row goes back to one note
long, on its own note of the scale. The steps behind it climb the scale from
there, so lengthening a row after a reset gives you a scale run. There is no
undo, so save the session first if you want to keep what you had. (SHIFT + MUTE
and SHIFT + SOLO do nothing on this view: see [Reset and randomise](/documentation/MSEQ/reset).)

Switch the global scale between major and minor and your patterns move with
it: each note keeps its place in the scale, so the shape of the pattern stays
the same.

If the sequencer follows a chord progression, set the chord-adjustment
selector to **Diatonic** (see
[Scale mode](/documentation/MSEQ/chords-and-scales#scale-mode-rhs-rows-78-cols-78)) to keep
your note arps in the scale as the chords change. In the other modes the whole
pattern shifts with the chord, and can land on notes outside the scale.
